items.note: S1.1 says a fixed linear network exchanges two banks with signs and restores auxiliary values, but gives no gates, no eight-row schedule, no (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and no three-stage composition.
S1.1 names frames D_v that change representation along edges so intermediate frames cancel, but does not state the edge operator D_vD_u^{-1} or the endpoint identity D_out S D_in^{-1}.
S1.3 alludes to nested subspaces of an m-dimensional space built from triple intersections, but gives no labels, no L=Ich, no sum Wm-2N+2L and no L<N/2.

S1.2 gives the endpoint shear (H,D)->(H+D,D) and S1.3 (via its quote of line 1152) gives s_b<W_b m, but the projection matrices with endpoint difference I_m and the rank sum s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b are missing.
Only the phrase 'with phase frames' in S1.6's method; no C_U, no translation kernels per residual vector, no s_c and no C^{tensor m} on every role.
S1.3 states s<Wm and S1.4 quotes 0<tau=sigma<1, but the reason (L<N/2), the deficits eta_b, eta_c and the explicit exponent 1-2^{-50} are absent.
S0.2 says moving one fixed-radix digit takes a bounded number of scans (quoting line 494), but lists none of the operations and omits the controlled-shift lemma.
S1.2 names lower-triangular factorization and quotes 'exactly a interchanges', but does not state A=E_1 Pi E_2 or that a rank-a edge shear costs a interchanges plus O(V).

S1.4 states s calls on streams of volume V/W at parameter e/m with a sub-linear power, but omits the recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), the O(V) node work, and the swap D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D that turns the shear into an interchange.
S1.5 states the O(Vu^tau) interchange of two u-bit address fields with fixed tau<1, matching Lemma lem:chunk-swap; no reduction to the power-width case is given.
S1.6 names phase frames and recursion, but has no change of basis P_M, no s_c child calls of C^{tensor f}, and no identity H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D.
No step concerns the packed selected-bit XORs or the bad-set repair.
S1.6 says the same strict saving applies to the numerical layer, but the recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), its leaves and the condition on lambda' are not given.

S1.6 and S1.6.0 state H_0 on one selected bit in at most d chunks at cost O(Vd^{lambda'}), and S1.6.1 gives exact Gaussian dyadics with one truncation. The route is the paper's, but the phase-frame recursion, packed bit changes, guard widths and error bound are missing, and the chunk width K and records are not specified.

S2.6 names synthetic transforms over C[y]/(y^r+1) with powers of y as roots, and S2.6.1 notes the retained frequency order, but F_t^+F_t^-=t^{-1}I, bit-reversed order, the layout L, the error and the cost are absent.
S2.6.2 correctly says ring products use signed packing and the established O(n log n) multiplier as a subroutine, but gives no evaluation point, recovery or cost.

The construction is there: two forward transforms keep their order through the pointwise product and the opposite transform consumes it. Missing are the normalization (f*g)/(rM), the commutation P(LBu,LBv)=LB P(u,v), the error and the cost.
S2.3 says resampling expresses source transforms through a power-of-two tensor transform, without the identity P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA, the contractions, or the conditions on s,t,theta.

S2.4 (Bluestein absorbs the target permutation into a normalized cyclic convolution) and S2.7 (the retained source permutation cancels, quoting (u*v)/S^2) give both halves, but the chirp a_j and the full identity are not stated.
Only kappa=2^{-182} and a 'compatible choice of rational parameters'; the sizes b,p,d,K,T, the other exponents and the prime source lengths are absent.

S2.2 says a Chinese-remainder map preserving convolution places coefficients on prime axes, but gives neither the map x->prod x_i^{mu_i} nor its triangular digit form; conservatively counted as mentioned.

S2.5 states that the twist turns the last cyclic axis into y^r+1 with the negative wrap undone by untwisting, but omits the map x_d->zeta y with zeta=e^{pi i/r} and the resulting identity M_C=(f*g)/T.

S2 and its sub-steps follow the paper's pipeline (digits, CRT, resampling, chirp, twist, synthetic convolution, permutation cancellation, recovery). Missing are the source transform's exact counterpart 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A = R F_s, the conjugation for F^+, and the rescalings by S and 2^{2b+4}S.
S2.8 states coefficient error below 1/2 and carry propagation to the exact product, but none of the error chain (E_s, E_w, 448b 2^{-b+gamma}) or why p=6b and gamma<=b/4 suffice.
S3 only asserts that every term of the cost table fits the bound; no normalized costs, margins g_i or min g_i=2kappa.
S0 says the bound disproves the n log n conjecture in this model and S0.1 recalls its origin, but the liminf formulation of the refutation is absent.

errors.says: For the bit procedure the endpoint operator is the address shear (H,D)->(H+D,D), implemented through lower-triangular factorization.
errors.paper: The endpoint shear H<-H+D comes from running the bit network with frames Phi_M. Lower-triangular factorization (Lemma lem:matrix-shear) implements each edge shear Phi_{A_e} with rank(A_e) recursive interchanges, not the endpoint shear itself (which has full rank m).

chain: At the top level the plan follows the paper's route to O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}): a fixed subset network with s<Wm gives two recursive tape procedures, and these speed up the synthetic transforms inside the multiplication pipeline. It thins out at the core. The dimension budget L<N/2 that produces s<Wm, the explicit exponents, the phase-frame recursion and packed selected-bit addition behind the butterfly layer, and the cost table with its margins are only named, so S3 asserts the final bound rather than reaching it.
